title: English File Intermediate, File 7: first and second conditionals, future time clauses

fixIt.text: If you study hard, you pass the exam.
fixIt.explain: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

fixIt.text: I'll call you when I arrived.
fixIt.explain: After when, as soon as, until: present for the future.

fixIt.text: We won't start until everybody get here.
As soon as she finish her exams, she'll go on holiday.
fixIt.explain: as soon as + present simple, with -s for she.

fixIt.text: Unless it rain, we'll eat outside.
If I had a bigger house, I will invite my whole family.
If we lived in the countryside, we would had a garden.
What would you do if you lose your job?
fixIt.explain: With would, the if part is in the past: if you lost.

fixIt.text: My parents would be happy if we visit them more often.
fixIt.explain: With would, the if part is in the past.

fixIt.text: If it rains tomorrow, we would stay at home.
fixIt.explain: A real possibility: if + present, will.

fixIt.text: You won't pass your driving test when you don't practise.
fixIt.explain: if = maybe it will happen; when = it will happen.

builder.text: If it rains, we'll stay home.
alternatives: We'll stay home if it rains.

builder.text: I'll call you when I arrive.
If I had a garden, I'd grow vegetables.
alternatives: I'd grow vegetables if I had a garden.

builder.text: Where would you live if you could?

radio.title: Moving out
radio.text: My younger brother wants to move out of our parents' house when he finishes university. If he finds a job in Phnom Penh, he will rent a small flat near his office. My mother says that if he lived alone, he would eat noodles every day. She is probably right. If I were him, I would stay at home for another year and save money. But he says he won't change his mind unless the rent is too high.
